description: A Middle Iron Age - Roman settlement with a strong focus on enclosures and structures interpreted to be a religious complex. Originally a circular stone structure and enclosure (uncertain date) which is interpreted as a shrine, this was made more substantial, and a second enclosure and shrine was built to the north in the mid 2nd CE. This continued to the late 4th CE, and produced religious material such as a figurine of Minerva and curse tablets. The shrine is thought to have fallen out of use at this point, but sometime between the late 4th and possibly the 6th (poorly dated), an adult male was buried at the centre of the primary shrine. Later the foundations and grave would be covered by rubble when the super-structure collapsed.
